chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa, Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Senani al-Mokattib, al-Hussein ibn Ibrahim ibn Hisham al-Mo’ad’dab, and Ali ibn Abdullah al-Var’raq - may God be pleased with them - narrated that Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Zakaria al-Qat’tan quoted Bakr ibn Abdullah ibn Habib, on the authority of Tamim ibn Buhlool, on the authority of Abu Muawiyah, on the authority of Suleiman ibn Mihran, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Muhammad, on the authority of his father Muhammad ibn Ali, on the authority of his father Ali ibn al-Hussein, on the authority of his father Al-Hussein ibn Ali, on the authority of his father Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them all).

He said: When it was time for the death of God’s Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) called me in. When I went to see him, the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) told me, ‘O Ali! You are my Trustee and my successor over my Household and my Nation both during my life and after my death. Your friends will be my friends and my friends are God’s friends. Your enemies will be my enemies and my enemies are God’s enemies. O Ali! Whoever denies your mastery after me, it is as if he has denied my Messengership during my life. You are from me and I am from you.’ Then the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) asked me to get close to him and taught me one-thousand gates of knowledge each of which opens up to one-thousand gates.
ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say to Ali ibn Abi Talib before his death regarding succession and knowledge?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Khisal underscores the doctrine of Imamate by presenting Ali as the Prophet's designated successor (wasi) and the locus of divine authority (wali Allah), where rejection of his leadership is equated to rejection of prophethood itself. It further highlights the esoteric dimension of Ali's knowledge, noting the transmission of a thousand gates of wisdom, which Shia scholars often link to the concept of 'Ilm al-Ladunni' and the esoteric interpretation of the Quran.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 28-43 Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa, Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Senani al-Mokattib, al-Hussein ibn Ibrahim ibn Hisham al-Mo’ad’dab and Ali ibn Abdullah al-Var’raq - may God be pleased with them - narrated that Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Zakaria al-Qat’tan quoted Bakr ibn Abdullah ibn Habib, on the authority of Tamim ibn Buhlool, on the authority of Abu Muawiyah, on the authority of Suleiman ibn Mihran, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Muhammad as-Sadiq (MGB), on the authority of his father Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir (MGB), on the authority of his father Ali ibn al-Hussein as-Sajjad (MGB), on the authority of his father Al-Hussein ibn Ali (MGB), on the authority of his father Ali ibn Abi Talib (MGB), “

When it was time for the death of God’s Prophet (MGB), the Prophet (MGB) called me in. When I went to see him, the Prophet (MGB) told me, ‘O Ali! You are my Trustee and my successor over my Household and my Nation both during my life and after my death. Your friends will be my friends and my friends are God’s friends. Your enemies will be my enemies and my enemies are God’s enemies. O Ali! Whoever denies your mastery after me, it is as if he has denied my Messengership during my life. You are from me and I am from you.’ Then the Prophet (MGB) asked me to get close to him and taught me one-thousand gates of knowledge each of which opens up to one-thousand gates.”
